text:
Anika: Quick one — we're polishing the session transfer confirmation modal copy. Need it short, clear, and screen-reader friendly. Thoughts?
Liam: Can you paste the current text?
Anika: Current: 'Move session to another workspace? This will transfer ownership and may affect access.'
Maya: Feels vague around "may affect access". Who loses access?
Sam: Agree. Also screen reader order: the visual header -> body -> primary action should map to SR announcement order.
Anika: Proposed: header: 'Transfer session', body: 'Move this session to another workspace. Members in the destination workspace will gain access; any external collaborators not in that workspace will lose access.' Primary: 'Transfer session' Secondary: 'Cancel'
Maya: That is clearer. Slight nit: 'gain access' vs 'will have access' — prefer 'will have access' for readability.
Liam: For SR, prepend a short live region string so NVDA/VoiceOver announce the consequence before the confirm button: 'Warning: transferring will change who can access this session.'
A11yTeam: +1 to the live region. Also recommend adding aria-describedby on the confirm button to point to the body copy; ensures the button reads the context.
Anika: Sounds good. One UX question: should we make the verb stronger for confirm? 'Transfer session' vs 'Confirm transfer' — which is more actionable?
Sam: 'Transfer session' is fine if it's the button label. Keep confirm language consistent across modals.
Maya: Also suggest an inline subtext for irreversible actions: small line: 'This action can be undone by restoring a previous version for admins.' if true. If not, say 'This action cannot be undone.'
Anika: Backend says we can restore versions for admins. I'll add: 'Admins can restore previous versions after transfer.'
Liam: Final proposed body: 'Move this session to another workspace. Members in the destination workspace will have access; external collaborators not in that workspace will lose access. Admins can restore previous versions after transfer.'
DesignBot: Checklist: short header, clear consequence, SR live region text, aria-describedby on primary, consistent button labels.
A11yTeam: Also run with keyboard focus order: focus should move into the modal, first focus on header, then body, then Cancel, then Transfer button. Screen readers often land on the first focusable; ensure the body is announced via aria-live or programmatic focus if needed.
Anika: Great — I'll update copy and the dev PR will include aria-describedby and a short aria-live announcement. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
